abstract: The nomenclatural status of the two octopus genera Bathypolypus Grimpe, 1921 and Benthoctopus Grimpe, 1921 has been the subject of considerable, at times contentious debate since both genera were first proposed. Of the two, Bathypolypus has nomenclatural priority, being the first mentioned of the two in Grimpe's cursory note. Although Benthoctopus was relegated to synonymy of Bathypolypus in 2002, the case for this synonymy was not compelling. The systematic complications generated by this act were subsequently aggravated by the description of another taxon, Muusoctopus Gleadall, 2004 (a replacement name proposed for taxa formerly attributed to Benthoctopus) and molecular data, that subsequently demonstrated Muusoctopus to be a junior synonym of Vulcanoctopus Gonzalez & Guerra, 1998. This created an untenable situation where multiple competing names were available to apply to many generally deep-dwelling octopus species with two rows of suckers, no ink sac, and either smooth or papillose bodies. Remnants of one important specimen historically attributed to the type species of the genus Benthoctopus (Be. piscatorum (Verrill, 1879)) are herein redescribed. Historical descriptions of this specimen are combined with modern observations and critically compared with what is reported for other North Atlantic Bathypolypus and Vulcanoctopus taxa to critique the original synonymy of Benthoctopus with Bathypolypus. The analysis demonstrates that the original synonymy of Benthoctopus with Bathypolypus cannot be upheld based on existing data, and the widespread nomenclatural repercussions of this status change are discussed. Finally, the type and only known specimen of Vulcanoctopus pseudonymus (Grimpe, 1922) comb. nov. is partly redescribed to facilitate a broader-scale revision of these problematic North Atlantic octopuses.
